edits.text: Keep a finite verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following phrase when that phrase is a core complement or clausal continuation (direct-object NP, essential PP, clausal complement, measurement, or other required continuation).
- Keep a numeral or quantifier together with the immediately following unit or adjacent parenthetical measurement that completes its numeric meaning.

- As a last resort, when other principles leave two candidate cuts tied, prefer a cut at a clear surface boundary (sentence-final or clause-closing punctuation, a closing parenthesis, or a comma that ends a parenthetical or clause) over a cut that splits a numeral from its immediately following unit/measurement or that separates a finite verb or auxiliary from the immediately following content token (direct object, essential prepositional phrase, clausal complement or other required continuation).

- As a last resort, prefer a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary (comma, semicolon, sentence break, or an explicit clause break) over a cut that splits a numeral or quantifier from its immediately following unit or measurement phrase, or over a cut that separates a finite verb or auxiliary from the phrase that supplies its core complement or clausal continuation.

- Keep a finite verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following phrase when that phrase supplies the verb's core complement or clausal continuation (direct object, essential PP, clausal complement, measurement); also keep a numeral or quantifier together with its immediately adjacent unit or parenthetical measurement.

- Keep a finite verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following phrase that supplies its core complement or clausal continuation (direct object, essential prepositional phrase, clausal complement, measurement or other required continuation), and keep a numeral or quantifier together with its immediately following unit or adjacent parenthetical measurement.
